A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EPIC and LegoLink. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original accuracy and latency experiments across six datasets and three LLMs, simulated serving workloads, and runtime analyses in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark, simulated serving, and runtime results in Section 5 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Core LegoLink is unchanged. For LegoLink-0, v2 Section 4.4 removes dummy tokens before linking, except in the first chunk; v3 Section 5.4 describes discarding their KV vectors during compilation without that exception. The unchanged results and lack of clarification leave uncertainty about whether this represents a procedural revision or a shortened description.

E1.justification: Both evaluate 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, SAMSum, MultiNews, HotpotQA, and Needle in a Haystack, with the same task coverage and serving scenarios. The expanded RAG discussion introduces no evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain FR, Naive, and the same CacheBlend variants. The asynchronous comparison remains LegoLink-16 versus CacheBlend-15, and long-context testing also retains FR. Newly cited systems are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v2 Section 4.6 states a 1024-token chunk size, conflicting with its Figure 7 caption's 512 tokens. v3 Section 5.6 consistently specifies 512 tokens, matching Figure 9. This corrects the reported setting without establishing that experiments were rerun; other principal settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 drops v2 Section 4.3's brief reported comparison of additional recomputation at initial versus alternative token positions. The plotted token-budget analyses, LegoLink-0 case study, attention maps, load and context-length sensitivity tests, and runtime profiling remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both asynchronous-performance figures report averages and standard deviations from five experiments. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Appendix A corrects the minimum CacheBlend runtime overhead from 17.68% to 16.37%, matching the MultiNews/Yi panel already present in v2; the maximum remains 63.56%. The corresponding benchmark and performance plots retain their results.

T1.justification: The attention derivation and complexity arguments are retained. v3 changes O = AVW_O to O = AV_expW_O, aligning the notation with v2's existing prose explicitly multiplying by V_exp. This repairs a notation inconsistency without changing the mathematical reasoning; no new proofs or formal properties appear.

C1.justification: The novelty framing narrows from introducing or uniquely proposing PIC to formalizing PIC and advancing prior work. The core EPIC/LegoLink contributions and headline improvements of up to 8-fold TTFT and 7-fold throughput remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds rationale for explicit caching and explains residual FR attention sinks through begin-of-sentence tokens. It removes discussion of chunking quality and self-contained chunks, drops the explanation that extra recomputation can hurt through noise, and attributes reduced accuracy to lengthy outputs more categorically.

D1.justification: v3 adds an EPIC repository link, explicitly documents zero-based chunk position IDs, and specifies maximum generation tokens of zero for KVCompile. Implementation and API explanations are condensed. Hardware, software versions, and the previously disclosed 200-case dataset sizes remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds a dedicated RAG discussion covering Adaptive-RAG and RAGCache, plus references such as DeepFlow, ArkVale, and RaaS. It clarifies PromptCache's position dependence while retaining CacheBlend as the central prior approach. Numerous other reference changes are publication or metadata updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, algorithm explanation, evaluation narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. System design moves from Appendix B into a main-text section, dataset characterization is integrated into evaluation, and the appendices are consolidated. Terminology becomes more consistent around compilation, linking, and immutable/mutable tokens.

P2.justification: All ten figures are retained. The architecture diagram is simplified and moved into the main text, as are the length-distribution plots. Diagram labels and captions are revised, including correcting AttnLink to LegoLink. The empirical plots retain their graphical results.

improvement.justification: v3 improves organization, adds code-access and compilation details, and resolves the chunk-size and runtime-overhead inconsistencies. These provide a limited gain in clarity and reproducibility. Deleted chunking caveats and ambiguity in the revised LegoLink-0 description are countervailing documentation losses; the underlying benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
